assertion_results.text: Step 0 extracts the Embargo policy URL from the Security Configuration as an optional field without raising an error (§1.71 — backward compatible extraction)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md Step 0 table line 19: '| Embargo policy URL | https://example.com/security/embargo-policy | Present (optional), so Step 1.7 is active |'. It is listed with the other optional fields (VEX Justification 'Present (optional)', and the unconfigured Upstream Affected Component field, which only causes a skip). Line 25 says 'Configuration is valid. Triage can proceed.' No error is raised.

assertion_results.text: Step 1.7 evaluates the CVE severity — CVSS 7.5 (High) meets the Critical/Important threshold (CVSS >= 7.0) and triggers the embargo warning gate (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: embargo-check.md section 2 table: 'CVSS score | 7.5', 'Severity rating | High (Important)', 'Trigger threshold | Critical or Important severity (CVSS >= 7.0)', 'Comparison | 7.5 >= 7.0', 'Threshold met? | YES', followed by 'The warning gate fires.'

assertion_results.text: Step 1.7 presents a warning gate to the engineer including the CVE ID (CVE-2026-31812), severity level, a statement about embargo risk, and a link to the configured embargo policy URL (https://example.com/security/embargo-policy) (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: embargo-check.md section 3 gate block: '⚠️ EMBARGO CHECK — CVE-2026-31812 (High severity)' / 'High-severity vulnerabilities may be under embargo. Before proceeding, verify with your security team that this CVE is cleared for public triage.' / 'Embargo policy: https://example.com/security/embargo-policy'. This covers all four required elements.

assertion_results.text: Step 1.7 requires explicit engineer confirmation (Yes/No) before proceeding to Step 2 — the gate is a confirmation prompt, not an informational message (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: embargo-check.md gate ends with 'Proceed with triage? (Yes / No)'. Section 4: 'If "No": stop execution ... Do not continue to Step 2.' and 'If "Yes": continue to Step 2 (Version Impact Analysis).' version-impact.md line 3 and remediation.md lines 3-5 make the later steps conditional on a 'Yes' answer.

assertion_results.text: The embargo warning gate does NOT trigger for Low or Moderate severity CVEs (CVSS < 7.0) — it is skipped silently when severity is below threshold (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: embargo-check.md line 20: 'The CVSS score is not below 7.0 (Low/Moderate), so the step is not silently skipped.' Line 16 defines the trigger as 'Critical or Important severity (CVSS >= 7.0)'. Together these state the rule: scores below 7.0 (Low/Moderate) are skipped silently. This is the rule as written; the eval's CVE is High, so the skip path was not exercised.
